newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Mizrahi to open up sale of subsidiary.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Mizrahi to open up sale of subsidiary.

text.p: Israel's United Mizrahi Bank will open up the sale of its New York subsidiary to more than one bidder, the bank confirmed on Sunday.

The bank had reached a tentative agreement in May with Brazilian banker Edmundo Safdie to sell him its New York subsidiary, United Mizrahi Bank and Trust Co, for $23 million. However, the two trustees who hold the shares in the subsidiary for Mizrahi objected to a non-competitive sale, bank sources confirmed.

The Israeli daily Ma'ariv said Mizrahi planned to hold a tender, but Mizrahi sources said no decision had been reached on how the New York unit would be sold. Ma'ariv said the trustees made their decision in response to pressure from U.S. banking authorities and from the Safra family, who control Republic New York Bank and are eyeing Mizrahi New York.

U.S. authorities ordered Mizrahi to sell its New York unit after a controlling stake in the parent bank was acquired by a group of Israeli investors in 1995. In the meantime, shares in the subsidiary have been placed in the hands of two trustees.
Safie had planned to buy the New York unit, which also has offices in South America, through a New York bank he controls, Commercial Bank of New York.
Mizrahi, Israel's fourth-largest bank, is 74 percent owned by the government. Plans to reduce the government's stake in the bank have been postponed.
